name: Nadab and Abihu
summary: Two priests, sons of Aaron, offered fire before the Lord that he had not commanded. Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them on the spot.
offense: The instructions for the incense had already been given, and given to their own father: Aaron was to burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon (Exodus 30:7-9). So the fault is not an error of enthusiasm but the offering of a thing expressly excluded. They took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not (Leviticus 10:1). The office itself was guarded to this degree: Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death (Numbers 3:10), so nearness to the altar was the most closely regulated standing in Israel and these two held it.
judgment: There went out fire from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord (Leviticus 10:2). The record notes what fire it was: the same that had come out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar in the chapter before, while the people shouted and fell on their faces (Leviticus 9:24). The fire that had accepted the lawful offering consumed the unlawful one. Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar were then forbidden to uncover their heads or rend their clothes lest they die and wrath come upon all the people, and the mourning was given to the whole house of Israel instead (Leviticus 10:6). The father was not permitted to mourn his own sons, because they died in the midst of the sin, and the sentence pronounced over it is the standing rule of the sanctuary: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified (Leviticus 10:3).

verses.text: And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.
And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.
Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died;

And Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord, when they offered strange fire before the Lord, in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children: and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the sight of Aaron their father.
And Nadab and Abihu died, when they offered strange fire before the Lord.

text.text: And there came a fire out from before the Lord, and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering and the fat: which when all the people saw, they shouted, and fell on their faces.

entries.commentary: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them. The instructions for the incense were already given: Aaron shall burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon. There were instructions on what could be burned and what could not; the strange fire is that Nadab and Abihu put strange incense before the Lord. When the Most High gave instructions through Moses on what to sacrifice and how, it was with specificity; you were to do it exactly the way he told you. They were also not the ones authorized to burn the incense; in the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to certain services and could not take a service upon yourself. Zacharias shows the pattern throughout the generations: he executed the priest's office in the order of his course, and his lot, his appointed job, was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord. The fire that went out from the Lord was the same fire that came out from before the Lord in [Leviticus 9](/bible/leviticus/9) and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar.
Then Moses said unto Aaron, this is what the Lord spake: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and they came near and carried them in their coats out of the camp, as Moses had said.

Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar were told, uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die and wrath come upon all the people; basically they were told not to mourn for them, because Nadab and Abihu died in the midst of sin and what they did was abominable to the Most High. The whole house of Israel would bewail the burning which the Lord kindled. Ezekiel is the example of that word: the Most High took away the desire of his eyes, his wife, with a stroke, and told him make no mourning for the dead, neither weep, and Ezekiel went and taught the people that morning, and at even his wife died. The same standard fell on Jehoiakim the son of Josiah: they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother, or, Ah lord.
They were not to go out from the door of the tabernacle, for the anointing oil of the Lord was upon them. The anointing oil had already been put on them, so they could not leave the sanctuary.

Some read this and think Aaron and his sons could never drink, but going precept upon precept, this speaks of when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation: they were at work doing the Lord's work, and there was no drinking on the job. Ezekiel lays out the priests' work rules. The priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, kept the charge of the sanctuary; when they entered the gates of the inner court they were clocking in, clothed in linen garments and linen bonnets, girded with nothing that causeth sweat; and going out to the people in the utter court they put off the garments wherein they ministered and put on other garments, like taking off a work uniform. Neither shall any priest drink wine when they enter into the inner court; that is exactly what verse 9 speaks of. They had to be sober minded because they taught the people the difference between the holy and profane and caused them to discern between the unclean and the clean, and in controversy they stood in judgment, judging according to the judgments of the Most High. On the priests' hair: they were not to shave their heads nor suffer their locks to grow long, but only poll their heads. Polling the head means keeping the hair trimmed and maintained; you can grow it, but keep it up.

Moses told Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar to take the meat offering that remained of the offerings made by fire and eat it without leaven beside the altar, in the holy place, for it was their due; and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place, the due of Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever. The wave offering is explained in chapter 7: his own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.

Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it was burnt; and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, because the Most High had given it to them to bear the iniquity of the congregation, and seeing the blood of it was not brought in within the holy place, they should indeed have eaten it in the holy place, as he commanded. Those were the instructions of the law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place, and all the males among the priests shall eat thereof; but no sin offering whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle to reconcile withal shall be eaten, it shall be burnt in the fire.

Aaron answered Moses: this day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering, and such things have befallen me; and if I had eaten the sin offering today, should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord? And when Moses heard that, he was content.

*1 And the LORD spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the LORD, and died; 2 And the LORD said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat. 3 Thus shall Aaron come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering. 4 He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on. 5 And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering. 6 And Aaron shall offer his bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make an atonement for himself, and for his house. 7 And he shall take the two goats, and present them before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 8 And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat. 9 And Aaron shall bring the goat upon which the LORD’s lot fell, and offer him for a sin offering. 10 But the goat, on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat, shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness. 11 And Aaron shall bring the bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and shall make an atonement for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock of the sin offering which is for himself: 12 And he shall take a censer full of burning coals of fire from off the altar before the LORD, and his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the vail: 13 And he shall put the incense upon the fire before the LORD, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy seat that is upon the testimony, that he die not: 14 And he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the mercy seat eastward; and before the mercy seat shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger seven times. 15 Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the vail, and do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat: 16 And he shall make an atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions in all their sins: and so shall he do for the tabernacle of the congregation, that remaineth among them in the midst of their uncleanness. 17 And there shall be no man in the tabernacle of the congregation when he goeth in to make an atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made an atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel. 18 And he shall go out unto the altar that is before the LORD, and make an atonement for it; and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about. 19 And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel. 20 And when he hath made an end of reconciling the holy place, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat: 21 And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness: 22 And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness. 23 And Aaron shall come into the tabernacle of the congregation, and shall put off the linen garments, which he put on when he went into the holy place, and shall leave them there: 24 And he shall wash his flesh with water in the holy place, and put on his garments, and come forth, and offer his burnt offering, and the burnt offering of the people, and make an atonement for himself, and for the people. 25 And the fat of the sin offering shall he burn upon the altar. 26 And he that let go the goat for the scapegoat shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward come into the camp. 27 And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung. 28 And he that burneth them shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp. 29 And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you: 30 For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD. 31 It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever. 32 And the priest, whom he shall anoint, and whom he shall consecrate to minister in the priest’s office in his father’s stead, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen clothes, even the holy garments: 33 And he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make an atonement for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar, and he shall make an atonement for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation. 34 And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. And he did as the LORD commanded Moses.*

Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

The Most High took the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix. The matrix is the womb; that is what the Lord calls it. All the firstborn are his from the day he smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Verse 13 proves the Most High does not love everybody; he killed all the firstborn of Egypt.

The children of Levi were numbered after the houses of their fathers, by their families. Your lineage is determined by your father, not your mother. The claim that identity passes through the mother is nowhere in the Bible; number the children of Levi after the house of their fathers is the standard of scripture.

Of Gershon were the families of the Libnites and the Shimites, numbered 7,500 males from a month old and upward, and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Depending on your family lineage you had a specific side of the tabernacle that you and all your descendants had to be on. The charge of the sons of Gershon was the tabernacle and the tent, the covering thereof, the hanging for the door, the hangings of the court, and the cords of it; that was their responsibility.

The ending "ites" denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath. They numbered 8,600 and pitched on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.
Eleazar the son of Aaron was chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary. He was the manager of the tabernacle.

Of Merari were the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbered 6,200, and they pitched on the side of the tabernacle northward. Their custody and charge was the boards of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, the vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins, and cords.

Moses and Aaron and his sons encamped before the tabernacle toward the east, keeping the charge of the sanctuary; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi that approached unto the tabernacle was considered a stranger.

All the Levites numbered from a month old and upward were 22,000; the Most High was separating the tribe of Levi unto himself instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. The firstborn males of the children of Israel were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen. A score is twenty, so threescore and thirteen is 73; the count is 22,273.

The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. Moses took the redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it unto Aaron and to his sons. The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

After the plague the Lord commanded a new numbering of the congregation, from twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go to war in Israel. Twenty is the biblical age of a man: Israel sent men to war, not children, so the numbering of them able for war fixes the age of manhood at twenty years old.

Of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites. The ending ites means the descendants of, the people you belong to: Israelites are the descendants of Israel, Edomites the descendants of Edom, and so it goes all down the line through the scriptures. Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. [1 Chronicles 1](/bible/1-chronicles/1) serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line.

Dathan and Abiram were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord; the account is back in [Numbers 16](/bible/numbers/16). The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign. Notwithstanding, the children of Korah died not.

Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan, and the families of Judah continued through Shelah, Pharez, and Zerah, threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred numbered. Do not hear Pharez and think the Pharisees came from the Pharzites; the Pharisees did not come out of that family. The rise of those sects is read of in the books of the Maccabees.

The numbered of the children of Israel were six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty. Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names: to many the more inheritance, to few the less, and the land divided by lot according to the tribes of their fathers. Land is how wealth is built, and Esau knows how important land is; that is why the land is kept in his generations and why Gad, the Native Indian, was never given one square inch of his land back, only the casinos and the little plots called reservations. Israel is getting the most fertile land back; as for this land here, let it burn.

Jochebed the daughter of Levi bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord; go back and read that account.

Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High. Christ said the same thing: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land; you must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas. Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
